title: The Order Window Merchandise Lines Are Counted Over for Circle Points
content:
## The window the merchandise lines are counted over

The merchandise lines billed to a profile under Northbeam Purchase Orders and Fulfilment are counted over one
of three windows when reward points on a Northbeam Circle Membership are worked out, and which one follows
what those orders carry.

1. Where merchandise lines were billed to the profile in the month ending on the handling day and a payment
   was taken on the profile's orders in that month, the merchandise lines counted are those billed in the
   month ending on the handling day.
2. Where no merchandise line was billed in that month and lines were billed in the three months ending on the
   handling day, the merchandise lines counted are those billed in the three months ending on the handling
   day.
3. Where neither of those holds, the merchandise lines counted are those billed in the twelve months ending
   on the handling day.

## The three windows as figures

| Reading | Window counted over |
|---|---|
| Lines billed in the last month and a payment taken on the orders in that month | 1 month ending on the handling day |
| No line billed in that month, but lines billed within the nearer window | 3 months ending on the handling day |
| Neither of those | 12 months ending on the handling day |

## Cases on the three readings

A profile billed 600.00 of merchandise lines in the month ending on the handling day, with a payment taken on
its orders in that month, counts that month alone: lines billed five months ago do not enter the spend.

A profile billed lines in the month ending on the handling day with no payment taken on its orders in that
month falls to the third reading, because the second reading turns on no merchandise line having been billed
in that month; the twelve months are counted.

A profile with nothing billed in the month ending on the handling day but 900.00 billed two months ago counts
the three months, and a profile with nothing billed in either counts the twelve months.
